summary: Raising the latte price from $5.00 to $5.50 reduced overall revenue by $12.75 despite stable latte order volume. Total visits dropped 6 to 107 and rival visits increased 8 to 123, indicating price sensitivity drove some customers away. The biggest product shift was croissant orders falling 11 while tea orders rose 5, suggesting customers cut back on food pairings or switched to cheaper beverages. College students bore the heaviest revenue loss at $34.25, while local residents gained $20.5, revealing the price increase alienated price-conscious younger customers but appealed to or retained higher-income locals. Wait time improved slightly to 5.5 minutes from 6 minutes, but satisfaction remained flat at 3.0, suggesting operational gains could not offset the negative price perception.
